chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Musa ibn Imran from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed Al-Nawfaly from Al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

A man from the people of Al-Qadar (those who believe in Divine Decree/Capacity) asked him, saying: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! Inform me about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah is due the Hajj of the House for whoever is able to find a way to it.' Is it not that Allah has made the capacity for them?' He said: 'Woe to you! What is meant by 'capacity' is the provisions and the mount; it is not the capacity of the body.'

The man said: 'Is it not so that when there are provisions and a mount, he is capable of Hajj?' He said: 'Woe to you! It is not as you think. You see a man who has abundant wealth, more than the provisions and the mount, yet he does not perform Hajj until Allah, the Exalted, permits him in that matter.'

key_terms.الْقَدَر: Al-Qadar (Divine Decree/Capacity), referring to a group or concept related to ability

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'capacity' (istita'ah) for Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the juristic definition of *istita'ah* by distinguishing between physical capability and the requisite material means (provisions and transport), while also introducing the theological dimension of divine permission (*mashi'ah*). This hadith is pivotal in Shia fiqh for establishing that Hajj is not obligatory until both external conditions are met and God facilitates the opportunity, a nuance often debated in discussions on the timing of the Hajj obligation. The dialogue with the Qadari highlights the interplay between human effort and divine will in fulfilling religious duties.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Imran, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A man from the people of (believers in) Destiny asked himasws, ‘O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww! Inform me about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:97] and Hajj to the House is incumbent upon the people for the Sake of Allah, (upon) every one who is able to undertake the journey to it. Is it not so that Allahazwj Makes to the capacity to be for them?’ So heasws said; ‘Woe be unto you! But rather, what is Meant by the capacity are the provisions and the ride, it is not the ability of the body (only)’.

So the man said, ‘So is it not so that when there are provisions and the ride, so he would have the capacity for the Hajj?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you! It is not as you are thinking it to be. You have seen the man with whom is the abundant wealth, more than the (required) provision and the ride, but he is not performing Hajj until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Permits him with regards to that’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Musa ibn ‘Imran from al-Husayn ibn Yazid from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Once a man who believed in absolute freedom of will ideology, asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, ‘O child of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, I have a question. Tell me about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, “It is obligatory upon people from Allah to perform al-Hajj who are able to do so.” [3:96] Has Allah not given them the ability?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Fie upon you, ‘ability’ means supplies and transportation and physical well being.’
The man then said, ‘Is it not true that when there is supply and transportation one then is able to perform al-Hajj.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘Fie upon you, it is not the way you think it is. There are times when a man has a great deal of wealth, more than supplies and transportation and still does not do al-Hajj until Allah, most High, grants him permission to do so.’”
